bib.title: Skill-RAG: Failure-State-Aware Retrieval Augmentation via Hidden-State Probing and Skill Routing

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Skill-RAG: Failure-State-Aware Retrieval Augmentation via Hidden-State Probing and Skill Routing", Kai Wei (Univ. of Michigan) et al. (7 authors), arXiv 2604.15771v4 (7 Aug 2026), preprint. No venue stated. Code: github.com/weikai202/SkillRAG.
COVERAGE: all 42,871 chars of extracted text, 15 pages (body is 8 pages; the rest is the appendix skill prompts and references, which I skimmed). Extraction is clean. I did not read the last part of the appendix (the remaining skill prompts) line by line.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Persistent retrieval failures are typed query-evidence misalignment, not missing evidence. Each type has its own fix: rewrite, decompose, focus, or exit. This is the paper's main argument, and it is mostly argued from t-SNE geometry (Fig 2) and the skill-usage distribution, with no direct causal test.
  number: none
  setup: Gemma2-9B, Qwen3-8B, Llama3-8B; BM25 retriever; 4-shot prompting
  quote: "Most persistent retrieval failures stem not from missing evidence but from a mismatch between the query and the evidence space."
  where: abstract
- The gain comes on out-of-distribution (OOD) multi-hop sets. Skill-RAG beats the probe-only baseline Probing-RAG by up to 13.6 ACC on 2Wiki (Gemma2) and 6.1 on MuSiQue (Gemma2). On Qwen3, the gain is 6.4 ACC and 5.3 EM on MuSiQue, and 9.5 ACC and 6.4 EM on 2Wiki.
  number: 13.6 ACC
  setup: 500 examples each from MuSiQue and 2WikiMultiHopQA; probe trained on 3,000 examples each from NQ, TriviaQA and HotpotQA; BM25; ACC is a separate accuracy metric next to Exact Match (EM)
  quote: "On Gemma2-9B, Skill-RAG gains 6.1 ACC points over Probing-RAG on MuSiQue and 13.6 on 2WikiMultiHopQA."
  where: §4.2, p6
- In-domain results are about flat and mixed. In Table 1, Llama3 HotpotQA EM is 23.1 for Skill-RAG against 31.9 for DRAGIN. Gemma2 HotpotQA EM is 24.2 against 35.6 for DRAGIN. In both cases Probing-RAG and Skill-RAG score below the plain baselines on EM.
  number: 23.1 vs 31.9 EM (Llama3 HotpotQA)
  setup: Table 1, EM and AC columns
  quote: "Skill-RAG 23.1 44.8" and "DRAGIN 31.9 38.4" (Llama3-8B HotpotQA, extraction merges the cells)
  where: Table 1, p5
- Accuracy gains over Probing-RAG on in-domain datasets are small, and rounds saved are modest. OOD datasets gain more.
  number: <1.1 AC points and <0.08 rounds in-domain. MuSiQue +5.5 AC and 2Wiki +8.6 AC, each saving 0.27 rounds.
  setup: averaged across three backbones; retrieval rounds per query (e.g. MuSiQue 2.05 to 1.78)
  quote: "In-domain datasets cluster near the origin (<1.1 AC points, <0.08 rounds saved); both OOD datasets occupy the upper-right: MuSiQue gains 5.5 points while saving 0.27 rounds, and 2Wiki gains 8.6 at the same saving."
  where: §4.4, p6-7
- The exit skill cuts rounds at a small accuracy cost on hard cases only. Hard cases are queries where Probing-RAG used its whole retrieval budget and was still wrong.
  number: 1.42 rounds saved for 0.6 ACC points lost
  setup: 2,660 hard cases, three models, five datasets. Exit rates: 13% NQ, 28% MuSiQue; by model, Qwen3 23.1%, Gemma2 21.9%, Llama3 19.8%.
  quote: "Across all conditions, early stopping costs 0.5–0.6 accuracy points relative to Skill-RAG without the exit skill, while saving 1.38–1.42 retrieval rounds per stopped query."
  where: §4.4, p7; Table 2, p8
- Skill mix follows query structure. NQ is dominated by rewrite (40%) and evidence focusing (35%). TriviaQA rewrite is 45%. HotpotQA decomposition is 45%. MuSiQue decomposition is 48%, and its exit share is 22%.
  number: 48% decomposition on MuSiQue
  setup: Fig 3B, averaged over backbones
  quote: "decomposition peaks at 48% on MuSiQue and 45% on 2Wiki."
  where: §4.4, p6
  Note: the paper gives two different MuSiQue exit figures, 22% in the prose and 28% in Table 2. The prose says "at 22%", while the later sentence says "ranging from 13% on NQ to 28% on MuSiQue".
- Too many skills is worse than four. Beyond 6 auto-generated skills, the failure-cluster structure dissolves.
  number: 4 skills vs 6+
  setup: t-SNE of hidden states for cases still wrong after 3 retrieval rounds
  quote: "Expanding beyond six auto-generated skills (D) dissolves the cluster entirely, merging both populations into an undifferentiated distribution."
  where: §4.3, p6
- Mechanism: a per-layer MLP probe on the final two-thirds of layers, sampling every other layer. Each probe is one hidden layer with a sigmoid. Probabilities are averaged, and retrieval proceeds if p < τ. No extra LLM call is needed for gating. The router, however, is a prompt-based LLM call that runs after a failure.
  number: none
  setup: probe trained on correctness labels from no-retrieval and single-step runs
  quote: "This mechanism requires no additional LLM calls and adds negligible inference overhead"
  where: §2.3, p4

LIMITS
- Only BM25, only 7-9B open models, and only QA benchmarks (NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2Wiki). 500 examples per test set. No variance, seeds or significance tests are reported.
- The paper does not give the threshold τ, or the retrieval budget or its calibration. Nothing is reported on latency or tokens. It counts rounds only, and it does not cost the router LLM call against the rounds saved.
- The authors concede the exit benefit "depends on data distribution and does not generalize to all settings".
- Future work is listed as ambiguous questions, conflicting evidence and domain-specific evidence formats. These failure types are not covered.
- The four-skill claim rests on t-SNE visuals, which are not a quantitative test.
- The probe needs a labelled in-domain training set and white-box access to hidden states. That rules out hosted API models (for example Gemini or Bedrock).
- Table 1 is mixed: DRAGIN or single-step wins some EM columns, and the "state-of-the-art" claim holds mainly on ACC and OOD.
- The EM and ACC numbers for Gemma2 and Llama3 on MuSiQue show Skill-RAG above Probing-RAG, but EM for the Probing-RAG Llama3 HotpotQA row is lower than the baselines, which suggests probe gating itself hurts EM.
- Some citations look misplaced (e.g. Asai 2023 cited for skill routing). Not checked.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Probing-RAG: Baek et al., 2025 (probe architecture, followed directly).
- Adaptive-RAG: Jeong et al., NAACL 2024.
- FLARE: Jiang et al., EMNLP 2023.
- DRAGIN: Su et al., 2024.
- Self-RAG: Asai et al., 2023/2024.
- Query rewriting: Ma et al., EMNLP 2023.
- Decomposition: Press et al., 2023 (self-ask); Khattab et al., 2022 (Demonstrate-Search-Predict).
- Evidence focusing: Yan et al., 2024 (CRAG).
- Hidden-state truth probes: Azaria & Mitchell 2023; Marks & Tegmark 2023; Burns et al. 2022 (CCS); Li et al. 2023 (ITI).
- Exit idea: Kadavath et al. 2022; Feng et al. 2024.
- Mallen et al. 2023 (when not to retrieve).

CODE: none. The appendix gives skill prompts. The router outputs one of `query_misaligned`, `multi_hop_missing`, `evidence_not_used`, `insufficient_evidence`. Prompt text is garbled by extraction (spaces inside words). Location: appendix A.1, p8-9.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p3), Skill-RAG pipeline: data prep, probe training, then the loop probe -> router -> retrieve -> probe. It shows the whole method in one view.
- Fig 2 (p6), t-SNE of hard-case hidden states under four skill settings (none, re-retrieval, 3 rewrite skills + exit, 6+ auto skills). It shows the cluster shrinking and then collapsing.
- Fig 3 (p7), A: rounds per dataset. B: skill distribution per dataset. C: AC gain against rounds saved, with OOD sets in the upper right.

NOTE MAPPING
- The strongest point bears on adaptive or conditional retrieval, specifically failure diagnosis after retrieval. It also bears on the pre-retrieval gate (whether to retrieve at all).
- Where it lands in the notes:
  - 07-rag-in-production.md, latency section: the "Router: skip retrieval for prompts that don't need it" row, and the RAGate paragraph that follows it. That paragraph only covers whether to retrieve, using a trained gate.
  - 11-retrieval-improvements.md: this note is an ablation reading. It covers CRAG (as a confidence gate and the Yan et al. 2024 evaluator), multi-query, HyDE, and a rewriter trained jointly in MMOA-RAG. The closest fit is the CRAG material in "What the ablations showed" (about line 44-53) and the "Pitfalls" list.
- Does the note already say it? Partly. The notes already cover "skip retrieval" gates (RAGate), query rewriting and decomposition (multi-query, TableRAG's decompose loop) and CRAG's evidence refining. They do not say that post-retrieval failure should be diagnosed by type and routed to a different fix. There is also nothing on hidden-state probes as a gate. Neither of the two notes mentions Probing-RAG, FLARE, DRAGIN, Adaptive-RAG or Skill-RAG. I grepped for those names and found nothing. FLARE does appear in references.md (line 101), pointing at note 01. So this is mostly new, with a sharpens link to the CRAG paragraph and the RAGate paragraph.
- Caution for the note: the paper's gains are on OOD multi-hop QA with open 7-9B models and BM25. The note's system uses an API model (gemini) and Bedrock KB, where hidden-state probes are not available. The portable idea is typed failure routing (rewrite vs decompose vs focus vs stop). The paper does not test that part on its own, because the probe and router are always evaluated together.

PROBLEMS: Extraction of Table 1 merges some cells (bold markup lost), so bolding and underlining cannot be read. No embedded instructions found. The appendix prompt text has spacing artifacts. Nothing was unreadable.
